## Accepted strong-expansion spectral partial, attempt 1/5

AIM Problem 3.2, High-dimensional phenomena in discrete analysis; corpus 20000886 / AIM-COMBINATORICS-0011, rank 1271.

The report proves a global host-class inequality for the strong expansion of C4 disjoint-union C5: for a bounded symmetric nonnegative r-kernel with regular pair marginal, the normalized negative fourth-moment budget B<=r-2 implies t_C4(U)t_C5(U)>=p^9. The arbitrary-rank L2 criterion yields the dense-host threshold p>=1/5 at r=3 for [0,1]-valued hosts with regular pair marginal.

The complete analytic proofs also establish the sharp binary r-lift threshold, safety of the full liftable binary ray and its finite tensor products, tensor closure and principal-restriction nonclosure of the marginal cone, and an irregular spectral negative control. Both the proof and audit retain their source-scope arguments for Lee's nested-link criterion and Zhao's closure hypotheses.

The original existence/converse problem remains unresolved by this work. No Sidorenko expansion of a non-Sidorenko core is exhibited, and no universal converse is proved. Spiro's compensated-core strategy is prior; probability and spectral ingredients are standard. Novelty confidence remains low and unconfirmed.

## Publication boundary and review limits

Exactly six authored proof/audit/acceptance and public-source-metadata files are added under `unsolved_math_prioritization/attempts/20000886/`. All analytic proofs, mathematical examples and source-scope arguments are retained. Editorial changes remove private workflow references and the numerical-exploration subsection completely. Only aggregate supporting verification totals remain as audit metadata; no optimizer output or other excluded computation is recast as prose.

Programs, checker outputs, fixtures, datasets, optimizer logs, copied third-party source bodies, source-derived images and private coordination/version identities are excluded. The edition is AI-assisted and unrefereed. Scoped acceptance is not external human peer review, journal acceptance, formal proof-assistant certification or novelty certification. Source inspection and retrieval are recorded historical observations; edition preparation claims no fresh scholarly retrieval, source-file rehash, source inspection, literature search or mathematical-program execution.

QUEUE.md and unrelated entries are unchanged. Editorial preparation adds no substantive proof turn and does not reset partial attempt 1/5. No merge, release, DOI or outside outreach is requested.

Base commit: `f6caddda8f8be2cdb3e91494325d8f7f365bc3fc`.
